created: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run directory was created
purpose: One sentence: why this run exists.
question: The question it answers, and what each outcome will mean (hit / exclusion / inconclusive), decided before running.
strategy: S-id from STRATEGIES.md, e.g. S3 (empty if none)
claim_ids: R-ids from the Results register that this run bears on, e.g. R4
command: The exact command line that performs the run, relative to the project root.

code_version.repository: path of the git repository, or null
code_version.git_commit: full commit hash, or null if not under git / no commits
code_version.dirty: true if tracked files had uncommitted changes, false if clean, null if unknown

file_sha256.code/example.py: SHA-256 of each code or data file the run depends on

packages.numpy: version of each library that affects results

external_software.Macaulay2: version and how it was invoked, for each external program

machine.hostname: only if recorded deliberately; null otherwise

parameters.example_parameter: every parameter that affects the result, or the path of a saved config file inside the run directory

seeds: every random seed used, in the order used
started: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run started, or null
finished: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run ended, or null
evidence_tier: NUMERICAL | CERTIFIED (the tier actually reached, not the one hoped for)

certificate.method: e.g. interval arithmetic on exact rational input; DRAT proof; exact rational dual certificate; null if none
certificate.checker: software and version that verified the certificate, and whether it is independent of the search code
certificate.location: path of the certificate and checker output inside the run directory

outputs: relative paths of every output file, with one-line descriptions
result_summary: What was found, stated at the evidence tier reached, with scope. E.g. 'Screen: 0 hits among 1.2e6 grid points in [0,1]^3; 312 points unresolved (solver timeout).'

accounting.unit: what one unit is, e.g. 'distinct exact objects certified' or 'random samples evaluated'
accounting.scope: which family, ranges and sizes the count covers; overlaps with other runs

notes: Timestamped notes: implementation failures and reruns, how to resume, overlaps with other runs, and 'superseded by runs/... : reason' if the run is later found to be wrong.
